title: Retail energy price deregulation (South Australia)
summary: ESCOSA stopped setting electricity and gas standing contract prices from 1 February 2013, when South Australia deregulated retail prices and adopted the National Energy Customer Framework (AER as regulator).

instruments.title: National Energy Retail Law (South Australia) Act 2011

commenced.what: Retail electricity and gas price regulation removed; NECF commenced in SA

direction_rationale: Removing regulated standing-offer prices is hypothesised to strengthen retailer entry and discounting (regulators judged competition effective), although outcomes for disengaged customers are contested.

industries.name: On Selling Electricity and Electricity Market Operation

comparison: NEM states that still had regulated retail prices (VIC 2009, SA 2013, NSW 2014, SEQ 2016; regional QLD, TAS, ACT still regulated)
confounders: NECF adoption on the same day
price_series: Electricity; Gas and other household fuels
notes: Deal with AGL to cut standing offers for two years was announced 19 Dec 2012 (secondary source).

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 14-15 October 2026 from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Removed regulated retail electricity prices once regulators judged competition effective. Prices can follow costs and retailers compete freely, though many customers who never switched stayed on high standing offers.

marks.reason: Retail prices follow costs rather than a regulated tariff.
Retailers are free to compete on price and offers; the gain is smaller for customers who do not shop around.

assessment.confidence_note: The archived econometric evaluation could not identify an effect on electricity prices.
